div.head: Ger 10
div.ab: [10] on hærfeste ripan, in Agusto ⁊ Septembri ⁊ Octobri mawan, wad spittan, fela tilða ham gæderian, ðacian, ðecgan ⁊ fald weoxian, scipena behweorfan ⁊ hlosan eac swa, ær to tune to stið winter cume, ⁊ eac yrðe georne forðian;

On hærfeste . ripan in agusto . 7 septembri. 7 octobri . mawan wad spittan. fela til||ða ham gæderian . ðacian . ðecgan .7 fald weoxian scipena behweorfan . 7 hlosan eac swa . ær to tune to stið winter cume . 7 eac yr | ðe georne forðian.

On hærfeste ripan, in Agusto and Septembri and Octobri mawan, wad spittan, fela tilða ham gæderian, ðacian, ðecgan and fald weoxian, scipena behweorfan and hlosan eac swa, ær to tune to stið winter cume, and eac yrðe georne forðian.

im Herbste ernten, im August und September und October mähen, Waid abstechen, viele Bodenerträge heimsammeln, Dach machen, decken und Hürde reinigen, Ställe herrichten und Verschläge für Kleinvieh[?] ebenfalls — bevor ins Land zu harter Winter kommt — und auch das Pflügen eifrig vollführen;

at harvest reap, in August and September and October mow, cut woad [with the round spade], gather home many crops, thatch and cover, and clean the fold, prepare cattle-sheds and pens for small stock[?] likewise — before too hard a winter comes to the estate — and also eagerly carry out the ploughing;

During autumn reap [fields] in August and September and October, mow [pasture], plant woad, gather cultivated products in to the home, thatch the thatch-roof, and to clean the fold and prepare the cattle-shed, and likewise the pigsty, before the harshness of winter comes to the estate, and also to go forth and to plough diligently.

During the harvest season, reap in August, September, and October, mow, plant woad, collect many crops for the home, thatch the roof, clean the fold, attend to the cowshed and also the pigsty before excessive winter harshness comes to the estate, and prepare the ground diligently.
div.note: ‘weoxian’ = ‘wischen’, to clean (Pogatscher: ‘wicker’, weave). Liebermann compares Gerefa 13 and 15, Rect 7.

note.seg: S. II S. viii. Das Wort scipena ist jetzt shippens ‘Kuhställe’

See Gl Waid. ‘to plant w. [wrong], bring in many harvests, bring them [? not in the text] under roof and [?] cover, clean stables’ [wrong] Sk-Wi.—In note r) correct to ‘H. flechten, S. h. und Schweinestall [ställe?] eb.’ as stated above II p. viii. The word scipena is now shippens ‘cow-sheds’
mit dem Rundspaten (unten 15) abschneiden (über das Säen: 12)

Dieser allgemeinste Sinn, wo cuman to tune, on tun gan nur ‘herankommen, eintreten’ bed. (gerade aus Kalendersprache bei Toller 1019 IV; Imelmann Menolog. 33), lebt noch: com gear in geardas übersetzt durch the year came to town Earle Beowulf 37, v. 1134; und Defoe (True born Englishman 1701) sagt, Wilhelm I. gab Land jedem Krieger, den he brought to town

This most general sense, in which cuman to tune, on tun gan mean only ‘to approach, to enter’ (precisely from calendar language in Toller 1019 IV; Imelmann Menolog. 33), still survives: com gear in geardas is translated the year came to town Earle Beowulf 37, v. 1134; and Defoe (True born Englishman 1701) says that William I gave land to every warrior whom he brought to town
Frondienste nach Kälte geregelt: Vinogradoff Villain. 296.—‘Boden [falsch] vorbereiten’ Sk-Wi
Labour services regulated according to the cold: Vinogradoff Villain. 296.—‘to prepare the ground’ [‘ground’ wrong] Sk-Wi
